texts.preamble: Valigi Venkataish vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 22 November, 2022 Bench: A.Abhishek Reddy, Juvvadi Sridevi The Hon'Ble Sri Justice A.Abhishek Reddy And The Hon'Ble Smt Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Writ Petition No.37105 of 2022 Order:
texts.facts: The case of the petitioner is that basing on four (4) crimes viz., Crime Nos.398 and 418 of 2022 of Shadnagar Police Station and Crime Nos.163 and 164 of 2022 of Shabad Police Station, the respondent No.2 passed the impugned detention order, dated 08.09.2022. According to the respondent No.2, the alleged detenu is a 'Goonda', as, he has been habitually and continuously engaging himself in unlawful acts and repeatedly indulging in the acts of goondaism by committing property offences such as robberies/snatching of gold ornaments from the women pillion riders moving on motorcycle in the limits of Cyberabad Police Commissionerate. He has been causing large scale fear and panic among the general public, thus adversely affecting the public order, peace and tranquility in the area. Subsequently, the AAR,J & JS,J impugned detention order was confirmed by the Government vide G.O.Rt.No.2079, dated 04.11.2022. 4.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the impugned detention order has been passed in a mechanical manner and without application of mind. Further, the alleged detenu was granted conditional bail by the Courts concerned in Crime Nos.398 and 418 of 2022 and the Crime Valigi Venkataish vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 22 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132740900/ 1 Nos.163 and 164 of 2022 were under investigation. Thus, as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order, the alleged detenu continues to be in judicial custody. Therefore, the apprehension of the detaining authority that there is every likelihood of the detenu indulging in similar offences, which are prejudicial to the maintenance of public order, unless he is prevented from doing so by an order of detention, is highly misplaced. The alleged crimes do not add up to "disturbing the public order" and they are confined within the ambit and scope of the words "law and order". Since the offences alleged are under the Indian Penal Code, the detenu can certainly be tried and convicted thereunder. Thus, there is no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention law against the detenu. Hence, the impugned orders tantamount to AAR,J & JS,J colourable exercise of power. The impugned orders are legally unsustainable and ultimately, prayed to allow the Writ Petition, as prayed for. 5. On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents supported the impugned orders and submitted that the alleged detenu is a 'Goonda' and has been habitually and continuously engaging himself in unlawful acts and repeatedly indulging in the acts of goondaism by committing property offences such as robberies/snatching of gold ornaments from the women pillion riders moving on motorcycle in the limits of Cyberabad Police Commissionerate and thereby acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order. Further, the alleged detenu was granted conditional bail by the Courts concerned in Crime Nos.398 and 418 of 2022 and the bail petitions moved by him in Crime Nos.163 and 164 were dismissed. Therefore, the apprehension of the detaining authority that there is every likelihood of the detenu committing similar offences is not misconceived. The series of crimes allegedly committed by the AAR,J & JS,J detenu were sufficient to cause a feeling of insecurity in the minds of the people at large. Therefore, the detaining authority is legally justified in passing the impugned detention order. In catena of cases, the Hon'ble Supreme Court had clearly opined that there is a vast difference between "law and order" and "public order". The offences committed against a particular AAR,J & JS,J individual fall within the ambit of "law and order" and when the public at large is adversely affected by the criminal activities of a person, such activities of that person are said to disturb the Valigi Venkataish vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 22 November, 2022 8. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has, in fact, deprecated the invoking of the preventive law in order to tackle a law and order problem. It was observed that every breach of public peace and every violation of law may create a 'law and order' problem, but does not necessarily create a problem of 'public order'. In Kanu Biswas v. State of West Bengal2, the Hon'ble Apex Court, while discussing the meaning of word 'public order,' held that the question whether a man has only committed a breach of 'law and order' or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the 'public order', is a question of degree and extent of the reach of the act upon the Society.
